accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT listed as a member of the Andhra unit of the Congress Socialist Party?
accepted.x: Alluri Satyanarayana Raju, Krovvidi Lingaraju and P. Sundarayya were listed as members. Tenneti Viswanatham was associated with presiding over the first session, not listed in this membership group.

accepted.x: He was jailed for publishing “Chicharapidugu”, associated with the 1857 and Manyam rebellion themes.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Madduri Annapurnaiah is correct?
1. He joined the Congress Socialist Party after the Salt Satyagraha.
2. He was the first Andhra leader to join Subhas Chandra Bose’s Forward Bloc.
3. He spent four years in jail during the Second World War.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Annapurnaiah joined the CSP after the Salt Satyagraha, became the first Andhra leader in the Forward Bloc in 1939, and spent four years in jail during the Second World War.
accepted.tq: Verify a sequence of political activity, affiliation and imprisonment.
accepted.sec: Socialist leaders of Andhra → role (Madduri Annapurnaiah, Mandali Venkata Krishna Rao, Kavuri Venkatappaiah)

accepted.s: Which of the following journals was edited by Madduri Annapurnaiah at a later stage?
accepted.x: Madduri Annapurnaiah later edited Jai Bharat, Navashakti and Velugu.
accepted.tq: Do not confuse a later-edited journal with the Congress newspaper he founded and edited.
accepted.sec: Socialist leaders of Andhra → role (Madduri Annapurnaiah, Mandali Venkata Krishna Rao, Kavuri Venkatappaiah)

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Tenneti Viswanatham — Founder of the Andhra Socialist Party
Madduri Annapurnaiah — First President of the Andhra Socialist Party
P. Sundarayya — President of the first session at Guntur
accepted.x: N.G. Ranga founded the Swatantra Party in 1959. Ranga, not Annapurnaiah, was the first President of the Andhra Socialist Party, while Viswanatham presided over its first session.
accepted.tq: Use the founder–organisation–year relationship and reject swapped roles.
accepted.sec: Socialist leaders of Andhra → role (Madduri Annapurnaiah, Mandali Venkata Krishna Rao, Kavuri Venkatappaiah)

accepted.s: N.G. Ranga founded the Krishikar Lok Party in:
accepted.x: N.G. Ranga founded the Krishikar Lok Party in 1951.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the three organisations founded by Ranga by their years.
accepted.sec: Socialist leaders of Andhra → role (Madduri Annapurnaiah, Mandali Venkata Krishna Rao, Kavuri Venkatappaiah)

accepted.s: The Peasant Institute at Nidubrolu was established during 1933–34 under the leadership of:
accepted.x: N.G. Ranga organised the Peasant Institute at Nidubrolu in Guntur during 1933–34. It was India’s first peasant training institute.
accepted.tq: Match the training centre with its organiser.
accepted.sec: Political summer schools and training camps → place + organiser

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the first political summer school and was held in the summer of 1937?
accepted.x: Kothapatnam in Guntur district hosted the first political summer school in the summer of 1937.
accepted.tq: Identify the earliest school from place and year clues.
accepted.sec: Political summer schools and training camps → place + organiser

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Madras Government lathi-charged the Kothapatnam political summer school.
2. Cases were filed in connection with the Kothapatnam school.
3. Tanguturi Prakasam protested against the government action.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Madras Government used a lathi-charge, filed cases and faced a protest from Prakasam.
accepted.tq: Check the complete chain of action, legal consequence and protest.
accepted.sec: Political summer schools and training camps → place + organiser

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

School or camp — Organiser
1. Madanapalle and Mantena vari Palem — N.G. Ranga
2. Hindupur political school — Idukallu Sadasivan
3. Tulluru centre — Annapragada Kameswara Rao
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three pairs are correct. Ranga organised the 1938 activities at Madanapalle and Mantena vari Palem, Idukallu Sadasivan organised the Hindupur school, and Annapragada Kameswara Rao was associated with the Tulluru centre.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure organiser–place pairs and check all three entries.
accepted.sec: Political summer schools and training camps → place + organiser

accepted.s: The six-week political training camps beginning in April primarily taught youth about:
accepted.x: The six-week camps taught politics and economics to youth.
accepted.tq: Identify the programme content rather than the location or organiser.
accepted.sec: Political summer schools and training camps → place + organiser

accepted.s: Who edited the Telugu journal *Udayini*?
accepted.x: Kompella Janardhana Rao edited *Udayini*.
accepted.tq: Direct journal–editor matching.
accepted.sec: Socialist journals in Telugu → editor

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: *Navya Sahitya Mala* — Vidwan Viswam and Tarimela Nagi Reddy
accepted.x: *Udayini* was edited by Kompella Janardhana Rao, not N.G. Ranga. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped editor while retaining the correct journal–editor pairs.
accepted.sec: Socialist journals in Telugu → editor

accepted.s: Which of the following journals were associated with N.G. Ranga?
accepted.x: N.G. Ranga was associated with *Navayuga* and *Prajamitra*.
accepted.tq: Group the two journals linked with the same editor.
accepted.sec: Socialist journals in Telugu → editor

accepted.s: Which statement about *Navasakti* is correct?
o: It was edited by Kompella Janardhana Rao and founded in 1934.
It was regarded as the first wholly socialist Telugu journal; another account identifies it as the first communist paper at Rajahmundry on 15 December 1937.
It was the Telugu translation of Gorky’s *Mother*.
It was founded by N.G. Ranga as a youth journal at Vizag.
accepted.x: *Navasakti* was described as the first wholly socialist Telugu journal in one account, while another identifies it as the first communist paper, published at Rajahmundry on 15 December 1937.
accepted.tq: Handle a source distinction carefully instead of treating socialist and communist descriptions as identical.
accepted.sec: Socialist journals in Telugu → editor

accepted.s: Raithu Rakshana Sangham was founded by N.G. Ranga in:
accepted.x: N.G. Ranga founded the Raithu Rakshana Sangham in 1934.
accepted.tq: Separate the year of the peasant organisation from the years of the rally and march.
accepted.sec: Programme - peasant, worker and youth organisation

accepted.s:
Which of the following represents the correct chronological order of the three peasant initiatives?
A. Ichchapuram–Madras peasant march
B. Raithu Rakshana Sangham
C. Guntur Peasant Protection Rally
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Raithu Rakshana Sangham was founded in 1934, followed by the Guntur Peasant Protection Rally in 1935 and the Ichchapuram–Madras march during 1937–39.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest year first, then place the rally before the later march.
accepted.sec: Programme - peasant, worker and youth organisation

accepted.s: The Kooli Rakshana Samiti was formed at Guntur in March 1935 mainly to organise:
accepted.x: Because the CPI was banned, leftists organised workers and farm labourers through the Kooli Rakshana Samiti, formed at Guntur in March 1935.
accepted.tq: Infer the organisation’s social base from its programme and political context.
accepted.sec: Programme - peasant, worker and youth organisation

accepted.s: Which of the following places was NOT listed among the centres to which the Kooli Rakshana Samiti spread?
accepted.x: The Samiti spread to Vijayawada, Nellore, Tenali, Eluru and Bhimavaram. Kakinada was not included in the listed centres.
accepted.tq: Check the membership of a geographical list and identify the extra location.
accepted.sec: Programme - peasant, worker and youth organisation

accepted.s: The Andhra Rashtra Yuva Mahasabhas were held at:
accepted.x: The Andhra Rashtra Yuva Mahasabha was held at Vizag in 1935 and at Kakinada in 1936. Annapurnaiah was prominent in these youth activities.
accepted.tq: Use the place–year pair and reject the reversed sequence.

accepted.s: The CPI was banned on:
accepted.x: The CPI was banned on 23 July 1934.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the ban date from the later founding and expulsion dates.

accepted.s: Why did Andhra communists initially join Ranga’s Andhra Socialist Party?
o: To establish the Forward Bloc in Andhra
To contest elections independently of the Congress
Because the CPI was banned and they were advised to work inside the Congress
To support the Quit India Movement
accepted.x: After the CPI was banned, Andhra communists joined Ranga’s Andhra Socialist Party on Professor Gout’s advice so that they could work inside the Congress.
accepted.tq: Link the institutional restriction with the strategic political response.
accepted.sec: Split between socialists and communists in Andhra → year + cause

accepted.s: Which of the following leaders was NOT included among the Andhra communists who joined Ranga’s Andhra Socialist Party?
accepted.x: Sundarayya, Chandra Rajeswara Rao, Krovi Lingaraju and Gadde Lingayya were identified as the Andhra communists who joined Ranga’s party. N.G. Ranga led the Andhra Socialist Party rather than belonging to this listed group.
accepted.tq: Separate the host organisation’s leader from the communists who entered it.
accepted.sec: Split between socialists and communists in Andhra → year + cause

accepted.s: The Andhra Communist Party was formally founded at Kakinada in:
accepted.x: The Andhra Communist Party was formally founded at Kakinada in January 1936, with P. Sundarayya as Secretary.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the month and year of formal organisation from the earlier CPI ban.
accepted.sec: Split between socialists and communists in Andhra → year + cause

accepted.s: Who became the Secretary of the Andhra Communist Party when it was formally founded at Kakinada?
accepted.x: P. Sundarayya became the Secretary of the Andhra Communist Party at its formal founding in Kakinada in January 1936.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of the office-holder at the organisation’s founding.
accepted.sec: Split between socialists and communists in Andhra → year + cause

accepted.s: The national Congress Socialist Party expelled the communists in:
accepted.x: The Congress Socialist Party nationally expelled the communists in 1940.
accepted.tq: Place the expulsion after the Andhra Communist Party’s formation and before the People’s War position.
accepted.sec: Split between socialists and communists in Andhra → year + cause

accepted.s: Which development widened the break between socialists and communists during the Second World War?
o: The CPI was unbanned on 23 July 1934.
The communists supported Quit India and opposed the People’s War.
The socialists dissolved the Andhra Socialist Party in 1936.
The communists supported the People’s War in 1941 and opposed Quit India.
accepted.x: The communists’ support for the People’s War in 1941 and opposition to the Quit India Movement widened the political break with the socialists.
accepted.tq: Identify the wartime policy difference that caused the later rupture.
accepted.sec: Split between socialists and communists in Andhra → year + cause
